The two-term matrix-unit evolution confines every matrix unit to a finite invariant triangular chain with all eigenvalues below one, so norm density plus unital contractivity proves convergence for every compact operator. Projections F_m retain an identity block through n<=m and attain norm one at each power. For E_pp, the isolated maximal eigenvalue b_p has normalized eigenvector with entries prod_{r=j}^{p-1}delta_r/(delta_r-delta_p); the top coordinate of E_pp forces its spectral coefficient to be one, proving the exact amplitude. Beta integration proves the parameter formula. The universal statements are analytical; 232 exact rational checks are supplementary.

value.rationale: The newly introduced family of unital completely positive maps has a natural fixed-point characterization but no supplied dynamics on compact observables. The finding determines sharp moment-dependent decay exponent and norm amplitude for every monomial rank-one projection over all admissible radial weights and a norm-strong-versus-uniform-stability dichotomy on the entire compact ideal. For the ordinary Bergman space the nontrivial exact factor (p+1)^(p+1) highlights substantial transient amplification relative to the fixed asymptotic decay rate. This quantifies a mathematically motivated gap rather than merely recasting the fixed-point theorem; no arbitrary parameter slice or routine numerical table is required.
